evals.prompt: Use the decompose skill on the csv-export feature run. Interview answers, pre-supplied so you don't need to ask: accept your recommended milestone boundaries and item sizing as-is; keep milestone 1 to a thin end-to-end slice.
evals.expected_output: breakdown.md in docs/features/csv-export/ with dependency-ordered checkbox work items grouped into milestones, covering every architecture component and PRD success criterion
expectations: breakdown.md exists in docs/features/csv-export/ with YAML frontmatter containing stage: decompose and run: feature:csv-export
every component named in architecture.md (Export API, Export Scheduler, CSV Generator, Delivery) appears in at least one work item
every success criterion in prd.md is covered by at least one item's acceptance criterion
every work item is a markdown checkbox with an explicit acceptance criterion (no item lacks an Accept line)
items are grouped into milestones and blocking edges between items are stated explicitly
the breakdown introduces no design decisions absent from architecture.md (no new components, storage choices, or delivery targets)

evals.prompt: Use the decompose skill to break the work down for the csv-export feature run.
evals.expected_output: no silent breakdown — the skill names the missing architecture.md and offers the two soft-gate options
expectations: the response names architecture.md as the missing predecessor artifact

the response names both soft-gate options — backfill via a short interview, or proceed while logging assumptions — and leaves the backfill path open (headless runs cannot be interviewed, so picking proceed-with-assumptions unilaterally is acceptable)
the skill does not refuse outright and does not silently produce a full breakdown.md as if architecture.md existed
if a breakdown.md is produced, its frontmatter logs the assumptions made under assumptions:

evals.prompt: Use the decompose skill on the csv-export feature run, and pull the project's open tracker issues into the breakdown as work items — backlog.md at the repo root is the tracker's open-issue list. Interview answers, pre-supplied so you don't need to ask: accept your recommended milestone boundaries and item sizing as-is; for an imported issue lacking an acceptance criterion, derive one from the issue text and the PRD.
evals.expected_output: breakdown.md in docs/features/csv-export/ whose work items include both backlog issues, each carrying its issue reference in the (tracker: #NNN) form and an acceptance criterion
expectations: breakdown.md exists in docs/features/csv-export/ with YAML frontmatter containing stage: decompose and run: feature:csv-export
backlog issue #341 is folded in as a work item whose checkbox line carries the reference (tracker: #341)
backlog issue #352 is folded in as a work item whose checkbox line carries the reference (tracker: #352)
every imported work item has an explicit acceptance criterion — including the item for #352, whose tracker issue records none (one is derived, not omitted)
work items not imported from the backlog carry no tracker reference (no invented issue numbers)

the breakdown stays complete: every component named in architecture.md (Export API, Export Scheduler, CSV Generator, Delivery) appears in at least one work item, whether or not a backlog issue touches it
